title: Typed and untyped constants
hints: An untyped constant like `const X = 2` adapts to whatever numeric type it's used with. A typed constant like `const X int = 2` behaves exactly like an int.
A typed constant also has to fit its type: 1 << 40 is far larger than an int32 can hold.
Remove the explicit types: `const Factor = 2` and `const TB = 1 << 40`. Untyped constants have arbitrary precision until they are used.
